table.html:
StepOwnerNotes
PlanAnaAll three steps share one change ticket. Approval from the security review board is required before any production access is granted, and every action must be logged in the audit trail with the ticket number, the operator's name and the exact commands executed.
BuildBen
ShipCai

candidates.idea: Give Step a little more room than in P while retaining most of P’s note width. This intermediate measure may improve the note’s line endings while keeping the compact lookup columns.

whys: The compact identifier columns give the shared note a comfortable measure. Labels are easy to scan, and the seven-line note remains continuous, though its wrapping separates a few related phrases.
The step and owner columns have a little breathing room, while the shared note remains broad and reads in seven natural lines. The three rows are easy to associate with their owners.
The label columns have enough room, and the shared note reads continuously at a useful line length. The compact table makes the three step-owner pairs easy to locate.

candidates.idea: Give the short labels their measured minimum widths and devote the remaining space to continuous reading of the shared note.

whys: The short labels fit cleanly, leaving the most space for the shared note. The table is compact and easy to scan, although the narrow Step column has little spare room and the note still wraps across seven lines.
The compact step and owner columns give the shared note the most space while keeping all labels visible. Its narrow first column feels slightly tight, and the last line is short.
The compact Step and Owner columns leave a comfortable measure for the shared note. All entries remain whole, though the first two columns feel slightly tight.

whys: The step and owner columns have comfortable breathing room, and the shared note is readable. The extra width in those short columns makes the note slightly narrower and its line breaks less flowing.
The shared note reads comfortably in seven lines, and the steps and owners remain easy to scan. The first two columns have some spare width that could serve the note.
The label columns have comfortable breathing room and the note remains readable in seven lines. Its narrower note column produces somewhat less natural breaks than A.

candidates.name: contrast
candidates.idea: Nearly equal columns give far more space than the short step and owner values need, leaving the shared note narrow and forcing many more lines.
candidates.label: bad

whys: The note is squeezed into 16 short lines, while the step and owner columns contain extensive empty space. It is slightly shorter than D but still makes both the note and the row relationships laborious to scan.
The shared note runs to 16 short lines, leaving the step and owner columns mostly empty and the rows unusually tall. It is slightly more compact than D but has the same reading difficulty.
The note is compressed into 16 short lines while the short step and owner entries occupy wide, mostly empty cells. The tall rows weaken scanning and visual balance.
The equal columns leave large empty areas beside short labels while forcing the note into 17 short lines. The resulting tall rows slow comparison and make the shared text harder to read continuously.
The narrow notes column breaks the shared paragraph into 17 short lines. Large empty areas around the short step and owner entries stretch the rows and make comparison slower.
Equal-width columns give short labels excessive space while forcing the note into 17 short lines. The resulting tall rows and large empty areas make the table harder to scan.

d1.purpose: Show who owns each step and the note shared by all three steps.
tasks: Find the owner of a named step.
Compare ownership across the three steps.
Read the shared note in connection with the sequence Plan, Build, Ship.
relations: Plan belongs to Ana, Build to Ben, and Ship to Cai.
The Notes cell spans all three steps; its text applies to the group rather than to Plan alone.
roles: The header row labels the step, owner, and shared-note columns.
Each of the three body rows identifies one step and its owner.
The tall Notes cell is a single group-level annotation.
keep_whole: Step names, owner names, and column headers.
Words and identifiers within the shared note.
may_wrap: The shared note can wrap naturally between words; its full text is not visible in the supplied overview.
same_scale: The three step rows and their owner cells should remain easy to scan as a comparable set.
The three column headers share the same structural role.
d1.h_vs_v: The short step and owner labels need little width, while the long shared note benefits strongly from extra width. A narrower note increases the height of the merged cell and the space distributed across its three rows; wider label columns can make row lookup more spacious but make the note longer vertically.

d2.purpose: Show who owns each step and the shared note that applies to all three steps.
tasks: Find the owner of a given step.
Read the shared note in connection with all three steps.
relations: The merged note applies to Plan, Build, and Ship as a group.
roles: Owner associates a person with each stage.
Notes holds a single shared narrative spanning the three body rows.
keep_whole: Individual words and identifiers in the note
may_wrap: The shared note can wrap at natural word boundaries.
same_scale: The step and owner columns contain similarly short lookup values, though Owner needs slightly more width.
d2.h_vs_v: The note is much longer than the lookup fields, so giving it more width reduces wrapping and the height of the merged cell. Wider lookup columns create a more spacious left side but make the shared note taller; its height is distributed across the three rows.

d3.purpose: Show who owns each step and the shared notes that apply to all three steps.
tasks: Find the owner of a step.
Read the shared notes while recognizing that they apply to Plan, Build, and Ship.
relations: Plan pairs with Ana, Build with Ben, and Ship with Cai.
The merged Notes cell belongs to all three steps; it is not specific to Plan.
roles: Owner identifies the person responsible for that stage.
Notes contains shared prose spanning the three data rows.
The header row labels the three columns.
keep_whole: The Step, Owner, and Notes headers.
Each step name and owner name.
Individual words and meaningful identifiers in the notes.
may_wrap: The shared notes may wrap naturally between words and sentences.
same_scale: Step and Owner are short lookup columns and should have comparable visual weight.
All three step-owner pairs should remain easy to scan across their rows.
d3.h_vs_v: The notes contain far more text than the lookup columns, so giving them more width reduces the height of the shared cell. Narrower notes leave more room around the short labels but increase vertical reading and may make the three related rows taller.

analysis.strengths: Fits the viewport, keeps headers and words intact, and gives the shared note the widest measure. The three step rows remain easy to scan.
analysis.faults: The Step and Owner columns are tight against their longest labels. The final line of the note is short, leaving an uneven right edge.
analysis.spatial_logic: Uses the minimum measured widths for the first two columns and assigns all remaining space to the spanning note.

analysis.strengths: Fits the viewport with intact headers and words. The first two columns have more breathing room, and the note ends with a fuller final line.
analysis.faults: The extra space in the short-label columns narrows the note without reducing the table height. Some phrases wrap less naturally, including the break between “production” and “access.”
analysis.spatial_logic: Reserves a little more space for Step and Owner while allowing the shared note to determine the height of all three data rows.

rounds.insights: The spanning note controls the height of all three data rows: both layouts need seven lines and produce the same row heights. Extra width in the first two columns is therefore useful only if its added breathing room outweighs the resulting note breaks. The quality of those breaks matters more here than maximizing width alone.

analysis.strengths: All text fits, headers remain on one line, and the note reads naturally without broken words. The first two columns are compact and easy to scan.
analysis.faults: The note is dense, though its seven lines are necessary within this width.
analysis.spatial_logic: The narrow lookup columns reserve most of the viewport for the shared note; the three equal-height body rows make its span clear.

analysis.strengths: It preserves the same readable note breaks, clear row structure and viewport fit as s0A.
analysis.faults: The extra width in Owner does not improve its short entries, while Step has slightly less breathing room.
analysis.spatial_logic: Two pixels move from Step to Owner without changing the note’s line breaks or the table height.

analysis.strengths: The compact lookup columns give Notes the most width, with every header and entry still fitting.
analysis.faults: The note ends a line with “is” and separates “exact” from “commands executed,” making the breaks less natural than in s0A.
analysis.spatial_logic: Reducing Step and Owner expands the shared note, but the wider measure changes its seven lines without reducing their number.

analysis.strengths: The lookup columns have generous space, all content fits, and the final line keeps “exact commands executed” together.
analysis.faults: The narrower note separates “production” from “access” and gives the short lookup entries more space than they need.
analysis.spatial_logic: Width moves from the long shared note to the two short columns, while row heights and total table height stay unchanged.

rounds.insights: All four layouts fit and have the same height, so the meaningful difference is where the shared note wraps. A little more width does not necessarily produce better reading: s0A keeps the lookup columns comfortable and gives the note the most natural breaks of these examples.

contrast.why: Nearly equal columns give far more space than the short step and owner values need, leaving the shared note narrow and forcing many more lines.

sameFunctionGroups.why: Both columns contain short lookup values, but their headers require different widths; each should have enough room for its own content.

synthesis.rationale: s0A gives the shared note ample width while keeping the step and owner columns compact and their headers intact. Its note breaks read naturally, and the three evenly sized body rows make the association between each step and owner easy to scan. s0B is visually very close; P and Q also remain readable, though their note breaks are somewhat less natural.

general: Fit short lookup columns to their content and give continuous prose enough width for comfortable reading.
Judge merged-cell text alongside the rows it applies to, including how its wrapping affects their height and alignment.
specific: All four candidates fit the viewport and produce the same table height and row heights.
The small width differences mainly change the note's line endings, not the table's structure.

synthesis.tradeoffs: A wider note column improves its line breaks but leaves less space around the short lookup columns. All four candidates retain enough room for those columns.
synthesis.uncertain: The preference between s0A and s0B is slight; their rendered differences are small.

critique.good: All text is visible, headers and names stay whole, and the shared note reads naturally in seven lines. The compact label columns keep the three step–owner pairs easy to scan while giving the note the most room.
critique.problems: The body rows are still tall for their short labels, leaving open space beneath each pair. The note begins beside Plan, so its spanning border is important in showing that it applies to all three steps.
critique.cause: The 312px Notes column is as wide as the viewport allows with the 56px Step and 69px Owner columns; the note's length still determines the distributed row height.

critique.good: All content fits without broken words. The wider label columns give the step and owner entries more horizontal breathing room, and the spanning note remains clearly bounded.
critique.problems: The extra space around the short labels contributes little to lookup, while the note takes an additional line and the body rows become visibly taller.
critique.cause: The 75px Step and 85px Owner columns reduce Notes to 277px, increasing wrapping and distributing more height across the three rows.

critique.good: The headers and all body text remain visible and unbroken. The large label columns make each step and owner easy to distinguish.
critique.problems: The short labels sit in disproportionately large cells, and the narrow note becomes a tall block of ten lines. The resulting vertical gaps make comparison of the three ownership pairs less immediate.
critique.cause: The 100px Step and 110px Owner columns leave only 227px for Notes, creating substantially more wrapping and taller rows.

critique.good: All labels and words remain whole. The equal-height step rows scan clearly, and the shared note is visibly grouped with all three steps.
critique.problems: The note occupies eight lines, making the body rows relatively tall and leaving unused viewport width.
critique.cause: The 280px Notes column is narrower than the available space permits; the Step and Owner columns already fit their contents.

critique.good: All content fits without broken words or scrolling. The seven-line note is easier to read, and the three equal-height rows keep the step-owner pairs easy to compare. The merged cell clearly applies to the group.
critique.problems: The step and owner columns are compact, but their labels remain legible and separated by padding. No consequential visual fault is apparent.
critique.cause: The 312px Notes column uses the available width while the 56px Step and 69px Owner columns accommodate their widest content.

critique.good: All labels and words remain intact. The wide note reads continuously in seven lines, and the step–owner pairs are easy to scan. The shared cell clearly covers all three rows.
critique.problems: The Step and Owner columns fit closely around their headers, making the left side feel somewhat tight beside the broad note.
critique.cause: Step at 56px and Owner at 69px are just wide enough for their respective widest text plus padding; Notes receives 312px.

critique.good: The lookup columns have comfortable breathing room, while all text remains intact. The shared note still reads clearly across the three rows.
critique.problems: The wider lookup columns introduce unused space and make the note one line taller. The resulting taller rows spread the three step–owner pairs farther apart.
critique.cause: Step at 80px and Owner at 90px reduce Notes to 267px.

critique.good: The step–owner pairs are clearly separated, and the shared cell remains visibly associated with all three steps. No words or headers break.
critique.problems: The lookup columns feel disproportionately spacious for their short values. The narrow note wraps frequently, producing a tall table and making comparison between steps less compact.
critique.cause: Step at 105px and Owner at 115px leave only 217px for Notes.

critique.good: All text fits without broken words. The lookup columns have comfortable padding, and the shared note is clearly grouped across all three steps. Its final phrase, “the exact commands executed,” stays together.
critique.problems: The three body rows are tall for their short lookup values, leaving substantial empty space on the left.
critique.cause: The long note in the 295px Notes column determines the combined height of the three rows; the 65px and 77px lookup columns use some of the available width.

critique.good: All text fits, the lookup values remain easy to scan, and the wider Notes column gives the narrative more room.
critique.problems: The narrower lookup columns feel tighter, yet the note still occupies seven lines and the table is no shorter. The last line, “commands executed.”, is isolated from “the exact” on the preceding line.
critique.cause: Reducing Step to 56px and Owner to 69px gives Notes 312px, but this width does not reduce the line count and produces a less natural final break.

critique.good: All text is visible, headers and labels stay whole, and the wide Notes column gives the shared prose a continuous seven-line reading. The three step-owner pairs are easy to scan, and the merged cell visibly spans all three rows.
critique.problems: The lookup columns feel tight, especially around the headers, and the tall rows leave noticeable space below the short labels.
critique.cause: Step at 56px and Owner at 69px are at their measured content-plus-padding minima; Notes at 312px takes the remaining width.

critique.good: The lookup columns have more breathing room, all text remains whole, and the merged Notes cell clearly applies across the three rows.
critique.problems: The notes wrap into eight lines and the rows become taller; the extra horizontal space around short labels does little to improve lookup.
critique.cause: Increasing Step to 76px and Owner to 89px reduces Notes to 272px.

critique.good: All text remains visible and unbroken, and the step-owner pairs remain clearly aligned.
critique.problems: The lookup columns contain large areas of unused space while the notes become a narrow, eleven-line block. The resulting tall rows weaken the table's compact lookup rhythm.
critique.cause: Step at 105px and Owner at 120px leave only 212px for Notes.

critique.good: All text is visible, words remain intact, and the step-owner pairs scan clearly. The merged notes cell visibly spans all three rows.
critique.problems: The Owner column has more spare space than Step, although both contain short labels. The notes wrap into seven lines.
critique.cause: The 77px Owner column takes space that could be used by the 296px Notes column.

critique.good: All content fits cleanly. The lookup columns have similar visual weight, and the notes remain easy to read across seven lines.
critique.problems: Step has noticeably more spare space than Owner, while the notes still require seven lines.
critique.cause: The 70px Step column is wider than its content requires; Notes receives 298px.

critique.good: The compact lookup columns keep each pair easy to find and give the notes the most room. All content fits, and the merged cell clearly applies to all three steps.
critique.problems: The Step column is snug, particularly around Build. The wider notes still occupy seven lines, so they do not reduce the table height.
critique.cause: Step is at its 56px minimum based on the measured content; Notes is 312px wide.
